findings.title: canManage() returns true for admins holding only the 'view' scope on Groups
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — it accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient for a manage-level decision. The no-arg canManage()/requireManage() is the guard for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`), so an admin who has been granted only the `view` scope on the Groups resource type (an all-groups view permission) will pass requireManage() and be able to create groups. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE, so this looks like a copy-paste of the canView() scope list. The new javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the same wrong claim ('Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups'), suggesting the doc was written to match the bug. Fix by checking only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE here.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission confuses authz resource IDs with group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the callback does `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. But per-group resources are created (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup) with the resource NAME equal to the group model ID, while resource.getId() is the separate authz resource entity ID. Two consequences: (1) hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing the entity ID never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the all-groups 'Groups' resource — per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never actually evaluated here; (2) the IDs placed in the returned set are authz resource IDs, yet callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) feed them into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, where the user provider treats them as group model IDs to restrict the user search by membership. When the set is non-empty (e.g. an all-groups view-members permission exists), the membership filter matches no real group and user search/count return empty results for an admin who should see users. The V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(...)`) and passes the Resource object directly. This should use groupResource.getName() both for the permission check and for the granted set (and skip the 'Groups' type resource itself). The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest does not catch this because the post-query `canView`/`canViewByGroup` filter masks the broken DB-level filtering and pagination/count behavior is never asserted.

findings.title: Group deletion fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V2 is enabled
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers a ProviderEventListener (whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, which V2 depends on) that on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent calls `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With the V2 feature enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and this PR adds the MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() override returning GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, etc.) unconditionally throws `new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The exception propagates out of realm.removeGroup(), so deleting any group via the admin API (GroupResource.deleteGroup) will fail with a 500 under V2. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the V1 GroupPermissions, whose setPermissionsEnabled(false) is a harmless no-op cleanup, so this is a regression introduced by the groups() override. The V2 class needs a non-throwing implementation for the removal listener path (e.g. delete the authz resource/permissions for the group, or a no-op), and the same applies to GroupResource.get/setManagementPermissionsEnabled which call isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled when the V1 management endpoint is hit with V2 active.

findings.title: No upgrade path: existing admin-permissions realms never get the Groups resource type and group scopes
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, and nothing else in this PR creates the newly added artifacts for realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change: the 'Groups' all-resource and the three new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, view-members. For such upgraded realms: (a) creating a group permission through the policy API fails because getScope() looks up scopes by name and throws ModelValidationException("Scope [...] does not exist.") for the group scopes that were never created; (b) GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` which returns null (the 'Groups' resource was never created), and then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `new ResourcePermission(resource, ...)` with a null resource, risking a NullPointerException on every group permission evaluation (canView/canManage/canViewMembers/etc.). A migration/upgrade step (or lazy creation on first use) is needed to add the new resource type resource and scopes to pre-existing admin permissions clients.

findings.title: Resources created by getOrCreateResource are never assigned their resource type
findings.body: In getOrCreateResource the newly created resource gets a name and scopes but never `resource.setType(resourceType)` (unlike the all-resources created in init(), which do set the type). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to enumerate per-group resources, so resources created for individual groups through the permission API will not be found by that query even after the ID-vs-name issue is fixed. The V1 GroupPermissions.initialize() sets the type ("Group") on its resources for the same reason. Set the type when creating the resource in getOrCreateResource.

findings.title: Javadoc errors on requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
findings.body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}" but the method delegates to canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. Additionally, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's javadoc says "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" while the method returns a Set, and its opening sentence references UserPermissionEvaluator#canView() although the contract is about group view-members permissions. These misleading docs describe the wrong method contract for an authorization-sensitive interface.
